modules.title: Simple moving average
modules.learn: The SMA summarizes the last N completed closes. A close above it is contextual evidence, not an automatic buy signal.
modules.question: With five completed prices, changing the lookback changes the average; which conclusion is justified?
options: A crossover confirms guaranteed follow-through.
You must declare the period and bar completion before interpreting SMA.
A single SMA level reveals whether institutions are buying.
modules.feedback: The average depends on the chosen lookback and completed prices. The indicator lags, and crossovers can fail.
modules.transferQuestion: A bar touches SMA during a choppy session. What should the learner check?
transferOptions: Treat the touch as guaranteed support.
Confirm structure, volume scope, and risk before considering a setup.
Assume the candle finishes at its current high.
modules.transferFeedback: The new context requires independent price structure and risk evidence; an SMA touch alone cannot qualify entry.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: A crossing only shows price's relation to a historical moving average; it cannot prove the next close will follow through. Confirm your setup independently.
An SMA is computed from observed prices, not from identities of buyers. It cannot tell you whether institutions supplied the trading volume.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A single touch of SMA is only a price/reference interaction. A setup also needs observable confirmation and risk analysis.
An unfinished candle's intrabar high cannot be treated as its completed close. Doing so would contaminate the decision timestamp.

modules.title: Exponential moving average
modules.learn: The EMA gives newer prices greater weight; its speed depends on period and seeding.
modules.question: Two EMA settings cross in a choppy market. What does the event establish?
options: The averages changed relative position but may whipsaw.
A profit is statistically guaranteed.
The next candle must close higher.
modules.feedback: A crossover states a relationship between two smoothed series. It has no guaranteed predictive outcome.
modules.transferQuestion: EMA9 rises but price loses a predeclared swing level. Which matters?
transferOptions: The EMA cancels invalidation.
The recorded swing invalidation still governs the scenario.
Only EMA9 can set the holding horizon.
modules.transferFeedback: A derivative indicator does not override an independent risk or structure veto.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: Two moving averages crossing does not establish a tested profit rate or a future fill. A whipsaw can reverse the relationship immediately.
An average crossover describes completed values; it does not determine the next candle's closing price or the size of its possible move.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A rising EMA cannot cancel a prewritten invalidation level. It is derived from overlapping price observations and may lag the break.
The EMA describes smoothed closes; it does not set the trade's holding period without an independent written plan.

modules.title: Relative strength index
modules.learn: RSI compares smoothed average price gains with losses. High RSI can persist during strong trends.
modules.question: RSI is above 70 on the available bars. What can Talia conclude?
options: Price must reverse on the next bar.
RSI shows strong recent upward momentum; overbought is not a timing guarantee.
A short order will fill at its planned stop.
modules.feedback: Wilder RSI summarizes momentum; an extreme reading cannot independently predict when reversal occurs.
modules.transferQuestion: RSI is 32 in a continuing downtrend. What is the defensible interpretation?
transferOptions: A bounce is certain.
The oscillator is low but the structure and invalidation still matter.
Low RSI means the seller is an institution.
modules.transferFeedback: Oversold is context, not an observable completed reversal.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: RSI above 70 can persist in a strong trend. The threshold describes smoothed recent gains relative to losses, not a scheduled reversal.
RSI says nothing about execution guarantees. Stops may trigger and fill at different prices, particularly across gaps or illiquid books.
transferFeedbackByChoice: An RSI of 32 measures momentum and need not lead to an immediate bounce. Support and resumption must be observed separately.
The oscillator does not reveal trader identity or prove that institutions are on one side of a print.

modules.title: Moving average convergence divergence
modules.learn: MACD compares faster and slower price EMAs; the histogram is MACD minus its signal line.
modules.question: The MACD histogram crosses above zero. What does this prove?
options: The MACD line is above its signal line under declared settings.
A position must be entered now.
The stock is cheaper than its intrinsic value.
modules.feedback: It describes indicator relationships under a period/seed setting, not a validated profitable entry.
modules.transferQuestion: MACD improves while the trade's risk level breaks. Which judgment is sound?
transferOptions: Hold because momentum is positive.
Reassess because the original invalidation was reached.
MACD eliminates slippage.
modules.transferFeedback: The documented risk condition cannot be erased by a correlated indicator.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: MACD crossing its signal line is a measurement, not an instruction to place an order. Price structure, costs and invalidation remain separate.
MACD compares historical moving averages; it does not measure cash flows, business valuation, or whether a stock is intrinsically cheap.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A favorable MACD is not an excuse to ignore a breached risk limit. An invalidation is a separate decision rule.
Slippage, spread and actual order fills do not disappear when an indicator line turns positive.

modules.title: Average true range
modules.learn: ATR averages true ranges that account for prior-close gaps; it measures magnitude, not direction.
modules.question: A bar gaps above the preceding close. Which value belongs in true range?
options: Only current high minus low.
The maximum of high-low, high-prior close, and low-prior close absolute distances.
The current close minus opening price.
modules.feedback: True range captures gap effects that a simple high-low measure can miss.
modules.transferQuestion: ATR doubles after a volatility shock. What changes in a plan?
transferOptions: Predicted price direction is now certain.
Volatility and possible risk-distance assumptions need review.
Liquidity and spreads are guaranteed to improve.
modules.transferFeedback: ATR estimates historic movement size, not directional probability or executable stop fills.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: High minus low omits price movement between the previous close and today's range when a gap occurs. True range explicitly considers both gaps.
Close minus open measures net body movement. It can miss the full wick range and changes since the previous bar's close, so it is not true range.
transferFeedbackByChoice: ATR measures prior movement magnitude, including gaps, but cannot establish whether price will rise or fall next.
A higher ATR signals changed variability; quote depth and transaction spreads still require separate measurement.

modules.title: Bollinger bands
modules.learn: Bands display a moving average plus/minus a selected standard-deviation multiple. Touches do not prove reversals.
modules.question: Price touches the upper Bollinger band. What is a defensible observation?
options: Price is high relative to this rolling band, not necessarily ready to fall.
A sell at the band is mandatory.
The band guarantees 95% success.
modules.feedback: Band contact is location and volatility context, not a probability promise.
modules.transferQuestion: The bands narrow during consolidation. What does this tell the learner?
transferOptions: Low recent band-measured dispersion; breakout direction remains unconfirmed.
The next move must be upward.
The watchlist is automatically trade-qualified.
modules.transferFeedback: Compression can change risk context but does not dictate future direction.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: An upper band touch can occur repeatedly during a trend. It is neither a mandatory sell instruction nor confirmation of a bearish reversal.
Bollinger bands use a rolling volatility estimate; a chosen multiple does not guarantee a 95% chance of a profitable reversal.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Band compression is a historical observation. The direction of any subsequent breakout must be confirmed rather than inferred in advance.
A band contraction is not equivalent to a successfully qualified entry; a watchlist and risk plan still have independent requirements.

modules.title: Volume weighted average price
modules.learn: This visualization uses bar HLC3 weighted by volume, an explicit approximation of actual transaction VWAP.
modules.question: Displayed bar-based VWAP rises while price crosses it. What is the right limitation?
options: The displayed proxy is not a venue-exact tick VWAP and a cross needs context.
The proxy identifies institutional order identities.
Any crossing guarantees a profitable continuation.
modules.feedback: The bar proxy is a learning calculation; feed, session and anchor decisions change its meaning.
modules.transferQuestion: A premarket VWAP and regular-session VWAP disagree. What must be checked?
transferOptions: Choose whichever best fits the later outcome.
State session inclusions and anchor before comparison.
Average both without considering timestamps.
modules.transferFeedback: Anchors and feed scope must be reconciled before drawing a conclusion.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: A bar-volume approximation cannot identify institutional order flow or counterparties. Trade and quote data still cannot reliably prove a trader's identity.
A VWAP crossing is an observation around a declared price reference. It does not prove future continuation, a successful entry, or a guaranteed fill.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Choosing whichever VWAP matches a later outcome is hindsight selection. The session anchor must be declared before interpreting a setup.
VWAPs computed over different sessions cannot safely be averaged without reconciling source coverage, timestamps, and calculation intent.

modules.title: Relative volume
modules.learn: Relative volume compares observed share quantity to a declared historical baseline, ideally the same clock time.
modules.question: At 10:00, 600,000 shares versus a matched-time baseline 200,000 shares yields RVOL 3.0. What does it prove?
options: Activity is three times this baseline, not whether buyers will win.
The stock will gain 3%.
A chart entry is confirmed automatically.
modules.feedback: RVOL measures activity relative to the denominator; directional thesis and execution require independent checks.
modules.transferQuestion: A platform compares 10:00 volume to full-day average. What is the issue?
transferOptions: No issue, the denominator is identical.
The clock windows differ and can distort the comparison.
The count proves a short squeeze.
modules.transferFeedback: Time-matched and full-session denominators are distinct metrics.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.
choiceFeedback: RVOL 3.0 indicates three times the measured historical activity, not a three-percent return. Volume intensity and price direction are different quantities.
A scanner or indicator observation never automatically confirms the required price trigger, actual liquidity, or a member's permissible risk.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Clock-matched RVOL and RVOL relative to a full trading day have different denominators; they cannot be treated as identical measures.
Large activity does not prove short covering. Borrow status, order-flow classification, and actual positions require independent sources.

modules.title: Discovery is not trade qualification
modules.learn: Discovery → research → watch → qualifying trigger → risk review. A scanner hit never proves a completed entry setup.
modules.question: A fictional symbol passes the scanner but its five-minute confirmation bar is unfinished. What state fits?
options: ENTER immediately.
WATCH / WAIT until the declared trigger completes.
Award a graded competency pass.
modules.feedback: Discovery does not establish entry confirmation or executable liquidity.
modules.transferQuestion: A candidate later jumps 12% after a NO TRADE decision. Was the earlier decision necessarily wrong?
transferOptions: Yes, all later winners had to be bought.
No, judge the original available evidence and risk vetoes.
Change the original timestamp.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: A scanner discovery lacks a completed trigger and has not passed a separate execution-risk review. An entry would rely on unobserved future evidence.
Fictional watchlist self-checks cannot award scored Lab credit. The learner is explaining candidate state, not satisfying a protected rubric.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A profitable future move does not make an unconfirmed prior trigger valid. Judge the earlier decision using evidence known at the time.
Changing the recorded decision timestamp after seeing the outcome is data leakage and undermines any meaningful strategy review.

modules.title: Premarket candidate verification
modules.learn: Separate premarket trades, regular-hours opening auction, corporate-action adjustments, spread and verified catalyst publication.
modules.question: A large premarket gap lacks a verified issuer filing and has a wide spread. What follows?
options: Qualified breakout trade.
RESEARCH / WAIT with explicit missing evidence.
Guaranteed opening continuation.
modules.feedback: An impressive gap is discovery; source and liquidity checks remain required.
modules.transferQuestion: A reverse split makes an unadjusted premarket gap appear dramatic. What next?
transferOptions: Reconcile adjusted prices and share identity.
Use raw chart highs from any date.
Treat the split as strong earnings.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: Price movement without verified issuer news, adjusted-gap reconciliation, and acceptable spread is still discovery or pending research, not a qualified breakout.
A large gap does not guarantee opening continuation; thin premarket trades and the opening auction can behave very differently.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Raw pre-split and post-split price references are not directly comparable; reconcile corporate action adjustment before calling it a gap.
A split is a share-capital change, not itself a positive earnings report or a validated demand catalyst.

modules.title: Matched-clock volume filters
modules.learn: Require same-clock cumulative volume comparisons with explicit historical session and sampling rules.
modules.question: RVOL 3.0 appears from 10:00-to-full-day comparison. What is the risk?
options: No risk, all denominators are equivalent.
The denominator mismatch may overstate or understate unusual trading.
A bullish entry is guaranteed.
modules.feedback: Use comparable elapsed periods and data scope; do not turn volume into direction.
modules.transferQuestion: Matched-time RVOL is high but quote spread fails the threshold. What now?
transferOptions: Hard liquidity veto still applies.
High RVOL replaces quote checks.
Ignore the bid/ask.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: A 10:00 cumulative volume sample and a full-session reference cover different clock durations. The mismatched denominator undermines an RVOL claim.
Relative volume describes activity. A calculated high value cannot guarantee upward direction, continuation, or a profitable entry.
transferFeedbackByChoice: High volume does not remove a hard execution-cost veto. A wide spread can make a promising candidate ineligible for the written setup.
Bid and ask prices and depth are material for possible fills; they cannot be omitted merely because RVOL is elevated.

modules.title: Spread and depth veto
modules.learn: Use quoted spread and time-stamped depth alongside realized activity; volume totals do not promise execution.
modules.question: Scanner signal is strong but spread exceeds the written maximum. What is justified?
options: Hard NO TRADE for that setup.
Entry because three indicators agree.
Assume the spread will vanish at fill.
modules.feedback: Execution risk is a hard gate, not a soft score. A wide quoted spread can invalidate a planned entry despite favorable technical signals; verify liquidity and potential slippage before promoting the candidate.
modules.transferQuestion: A displayed ask contains only 200 shares and planned size is 1,000. What can be assumed?
transferOptions: Full order fills at one displayed ask price.
Nothing about the whole fill price; book may change.
A stop guarantees loss ceiling.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: Technical indicators are supporting context, not permission to override a predeclared spread or liquidity veto. Execution cost remains a hard gate.
Visible spreads can change at execution, but you cannot assume they will vanish in time to save a trade plan that currently fails its cost threshold.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Displayed ask size is an observed quote, not a guarantee that an entire larger order can execute at that same price.
A stop instruction can trigger without filling at the reference price; modeled price distance is not a guaranteed loss ceiling.

modules.title: Primary-source catalyst queue
modules.learn: Verify company identity, original document and publicly available timestamp before classifying news.
modules.question: An online article is dated after the replay decision timestamp. Can it support the earlier decision?
options: No, publication later cannot justify prior knowledge.
Yes, later news is always known.
Only if the price later rose.
modules.feedback: No-lookahead chronology is more important than hindsight narratives.
modules.transferQuestion: A social post cites earnings but no issuer release is available. What is the state?
transferOptions: Verifiably catalyst-qualified.
VERIFY_PENDING until primary source and time match.
A confirmed market order.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: An article published after the replay pause was not publicly available at that decision timestamp. Using it would introduce lookahead bias.
An eventual rally cannot justify an earlier decision with news unavailable at the time. Evidence chronology must remain independent of outcome.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A social claim without a primary issuer document or timestamp remains pending verification. It cannot qualify a source-driven catalyst lane.
An unverified headline and an actual broker order are different things. Neither requires the other to exist or be correct.

modules.title: Journal rejected candidates
modules.learn: Log the missing condition, actual decision timestamp and subsequent outcome separately; do not grade no-trades by later winners.
modules.question: A stock rallies after you rejected it for a predeclared wide-spread veto. What should be recorded?
options: Rewrite the earlier decision as a mistake.
Keep the original valid veto and analyze the later move separately.
Delete the stop and entry rules.
modules.feedback: The later move is an outcome, not proof that the earlier unsupported entry was justified.
modules.transferQuestion: What documented evidence makes a NO TRADE decision complete and reviewable without hindsight?
transferOptions: A recorded condition, observation time and reason for rejection.
A forecast of guaranteed future loss.
No documentation.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.
choiceFeedback: A later price increase cannot retroactively erase an earlier spread veto. Preserve the as-of-time decision and evaluate subsequent prices separately.
Deleting an entry or risk condition destroys the audit trail. A useful NO TRADE journal preserves the original source, time and reason.
transferFeedbackByChoice: The fact that the instrument later fell or rallied cannot make the original recorded criteria disappear or retroactively determine a decision's quality.
A complete NO TRADE decision needs evidence, a timestamp and an articulated violated gate; an undocumented prediction is insufficient.

modules.title: On-Balance Volume
modules.learn: OBV adds a completed bar's share volume when its close exceeds the previous close and subtracts it when the close falls; no change means zero addition. Its starting value is arbitrary.
modules.why: OBV can describe whether volume coincides with closing-price direction but cannot reveal who traded.
modules.method: Compare adjacent completed closes, accumulate plus or minus volume, and interpret changes rather than the arbitrary starting total.
modules.limitation: A large bar can dominate OBV. It is not an order-flow aggressor classifier.
modules.question: What does OBV add when the completed close rises with 12,000 shares?
options: 12,000 shares to the prior OBV balance.
12,000 confirmed institutional purchases.
A guaranteed $12,000 future price advance.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: 12,000 shares to the prior OBV balance. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.
modules.transferQuestion: Why can a failed resistance close overrule a favorable OBV slope?
transferOptions: OBV is a binding risk limit.
Confirmed price invalidation still governs the setup.
OBV proves short covering.
modules.transferFeedback: In this changed case, the evidence supports: Confirmed price invalidation still governs the setup. Separate observable source facts from assumptions and review risk before any hypothetical trade.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars. Calculations do not use unrevealed bars, live quotes, grades, or trade orders.
choiceFeedback: The statement “12,000 confirmed institutional purchases.” does not follow from the defined evidence. 12,000 shares to the prior OBV balance. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “A guaranteed $12,000 future price advance.” does not follow from the defined evidence. 12,000 shares to the prior OBV balance. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.
transferFeedbackByChoice: The statement “OBV is a binding risk limit.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Confirmed price invalidation still governs the setup. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “OBV proves short covering.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Confirmed price invalidation still governs the setup. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.
modules.scaffold: Find the declared source, timeframe and calculation first. Compare adjacent completed closes, accumulate plus or minus volume, and interpret changes rather than the arbitrary starting total. The defensible answer is the one that does not promise future prices or waive hard gates.

modules.title: Chaikin Money Flow
modules.learn: CMF weights each bar's volume by its closing location within the high-low range, then divides the signed total by all shares over the selected completed-bar window.
modules.why: CMF summarizes closing-location behavior under volume, not the identity of buyers or cash moving into accounts.
modules.method: Compute (2×close−high−low)/(high−low) for each bar; zero-range bars contribute zero signed flow. Sum value×volume and divide by summed volume.
modules.limitation: The prior-close gap is not part of the close-location multiplier and can change the larger chart context.
modules.question: At the exact midpoint of a candle's high-low range, what is its CMF close-location multiplier?
options: Positive one for bullish volume.
Zero because the close is midrange.
Negative one because sellers dominate.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Zero because the close is midrange. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.
modules.transferQuestion: After an overnight price gap, CMF is near zero. Which interpretation is strongest?
transferOptions: The gap did not occur.
CMF proves all traders are neutral.
The bar-based CMF may miss the gap; verify price structure separately.
modules.transferFeedback: In this changed case, the evidence supports: The bar-based CMF may miss the gap; verify price structure separately. Separate observable source facts from assumptions and review risk before any hypothetical trade.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars. Calculations do not use unrevealed bars, live quotes, grades, or trade orders.
choiceFeedback: The statement “Positive one for bullish volume.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Zero because the close is midrange. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “Negative one because sellers dominate.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Zero because the close is midrange. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.
transferFeedbackByChoice: The statement “The gap did not occur.” does not follow from the defined evidence. The bar-based CMF may miss the gap; verify price structure separately. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “CMF proves all traders are neutral.” does not follow from the defined evidence. The bar-based CMF may miss the gap; verify price structure separately. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.
modules.scaffold: Find the declared source, timeframe and calculation first. Compute (2×close−high−low)/(high−low) for each bar; zero-range bars contribute zero signed flow. Sum value×volume and divide by summed volume. The defensible answer is the one that does not promise future prices or waive hard gates.

modules.title: Money Flow Index
modules.learn: MFI is a bounded oscillator combining typical-price direction with volume-weighted flow over a chosen completed-bar window.
modules.why: It can help compare price and participation momentum while remaining distinct from actual identified institutional cash flows.
modules.method: Classify each current typical-price×volume as positive, negative or neutral relative to the prior typical price. Compute 100−100/(1+positive/negative), handling zero denominators.
modules.limitation: High MFI can remain elevated in trends, and the algorithm cannot name transaction counterparties.
modules.question: What does an elevated MFI reading establish by itself?
options: Certain bearish reversal on the next bar.
Strong recent typical-price/volume momentum without a reversal guarantee.
Identified net institutional purchases.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Strong recent typical-price/volume momentum without a reversal guarantee. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.
modules.transferQuestion: What must MFI do when positive flow exists but negative flow equals zero?
transferOptions: Handle the zero denominator, conventionally producing 100.
Produce a negative unlimited value.
Assume execution at the midquote.
modules.transferFeedback: In this changed case, the evidence supports: Handle the zero denominator, conventionally producing 100. Separate observable source facts from assumptions and review risk before any hypothetical trade.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars. Calculations do not use unrevealed bars, live quotes, grades, or trade orders.
choiceFeedback: The statement “Certain bearish reversal on the next bar.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Strong recent typical-price/volume momentum without a reversal guarantee. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “Identified net institutional purchases.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Strong recent typical-price/volume momentum without a reversal guarantee. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.
transferFeedbackByChoice: The statement “Produce a negative unlimited value.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Handle the zero denominator, conventionally producing 100. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

The statement “Assume execution at the midquote.” does not follow from the defined evidence. Handle the zero denominator, conventionally producing 100. The fictional scenario still needs independent confirmation and cannot establish a guaranteed market outcome.

modules.title: Price Rate of Change
modules.learn: Rate of Change compares the latest completed close with a close a declared number of completed bars earlier, expressed as a percentage.
modules.why: Normalized price change makes historical comparisons possible once the sampling interval and corporate-action basis match.
modules.method: Calculate 100×(latest close/close N bars ago−1) only with a nonzero, comparable historical reference.
modules.limitation: ROC describes a past return; reverse splits or mismatched periods can make unadjusted comparisons misleading.
modules.question: A closing price rises from $10 to $12 over ten completed bars. What is ROC(10)?
options: Positive 20% historical change.
A guaranteed 20% increase in the next ten bars.
Two additional shares issued per investor.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Positive 20% historical change. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.
modules.transferQuestion: How should a learner calculate ROC across a reverse split?
transferOptions: Use nominal raw prices to show a huge signal.
Reconcile corporate-action adjustment and identical bar windows.
Substitute an oscillator for the changed share count.
modules.transferFeedback: In this changed case, the evidence supports: Reconcile corporate-action adjustment and identical bar windows. Separate observable source facts from assumptions and review risk before any hypothetical trade.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars. Calculations do not use unrevealed bars, live quotes, grades, or trade orders.

modules.title: Donchian Channels
modules.learn: Donchian channels show the rolling highest high and lowest low of N completed candles, with their midpoint as an optional reference.
modules.why: They make a predeclared price-range boundary visible before evaluating a hypothetical breakout.
modules.method: Compute max(high) and min(low) within the declared completed-bar window; this exercise includes the current completed bar.
modules.limitation: A strategy using the previous channel must exclude the current bar; touching the channel never guarantees breakout acceptance.
modules.question: What does the upper Donchian channel represent?
options: Highest high in the chosen completed window.
A guaranteed limit order execution level.
Volume-weighted transaction price.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Highest high in the chosen completed window. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.
modules.transferQuestion: Why distinguish the previous channel from one including the current bar?
transferOptions: Both must always produce identical highs.
The previous channel uses an earlier fixed window for an as-of-time breakout test.
Future bars are always allowed in retrospective channel values.
modules.transferFeedback: In this changed case, the evidence supports: The previous channel uses an earlier fixed window for an as-of-time breakout test. Separate observable source facts from assumptions and review risk before any hypothetical trade.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars. Calculations do not use unrevealed bars, live quotes, grades, or trade orders.

modules.title: Keltner Channels
modules.learn: In this explicit Keltner variant, an EMA of completed closes forms the center while upper/lower envelopes sit two ATR values away.
modules.why: This can show how an observed price excursion compares with a rolling volatility-adjusted reference.
modules.method: Compute EMA(close,N) and Wilder ATR(N) using the displayed complete bars; plot center ± 2×ATR. Other platforms may use different definitions.
modules.limitation: Keltner and Bollinger bands need not agree because the former uses ATR and the latter a standard-deviation method.
modules.question: EMA center is $20 and ATR is $1 with multiplier two. What upper band follows?
options: $22 under the stated formula.
$21 because ATR is never multiplied.
$20 because the next candle must be flat.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: $22 under the stated formula. This is an ungraded explanation of observations, not a guaranteed price outcome or order execution.

modules.title: Quote and Source Freshness
modules.learn: A source can be authentic but too stale for the declared decision time. Distinguish event time, provider receipt time and the learner's replay pause.

modules.title: Sector Benchmark Comparison
modules.learn: Relative strength compares matched-period security performance against a chosen market or sector benchmark; a green stock can still underperform.
modules.why: Benchmark comparisons can improve watchlist research quality without asserting future sector leadership.
modules.method: Compare consistent adjusted returns and sector membership for the same interval; a fictional ratio at least one passes only this contextual filter.

It gained absolutely but underperformed relatively.
It must lose 4% tomorrow.

modules.title: Short-Sale Eligibility and Halts
modules.learn: A bearish chart idea does not establish short-borrow access; halt status and applicable SSR price-test restrictions are separate from market structure.
modules.why: Eligibility research prevents teaching fictional short entries as if real broker approval and share location were automatic.
modules.method: Independently check documented borrow availability, no current halt, the setup trigger and existing liquidity/source requirements.
modules.limitation: SSR is not a blanket short-sale ban; short-side risks can greatly exceed a mirrored long-side chart plan.
modules.question: A short setup appears but borrow is unavailable. What follows?
options: The chart confirms automatic short eligibility.
NO TRADE for that short variant pending borrow approval.
SSR supplies a share locate automatically.

A favorable RSI substitutes for exchange trading status.
A halt requires separate status and reopening evidence before any hypothetical execution.

modules.title: Weighted Moving Average: Recent Closes
modules.learn: A linearly weighted moving average gives later completed closes higher weights than earlier closes. For length N, use weights 1 through N, oldest to newest; divide the weighted sum by N(N+1)/2.
modules.why: WMA makes the learner compare how two averaging rules respond to a recent price move. It does not independently prove an upward trend will continue.
modules.method: On a declared completed-close window, weight the oldest close 1 and newest N; sum close×weight and divide by the sum of weights. Compare it with a simple moving average only on identical dates, session and seed rules.
modules.limitation: WMA reacts faster than an equally long SMA for a newly shifted close, but both lag and can whipsaw in chop. Historical bars cannot identify a future close.
modules.question: Three completed closes are $10, $11 and $14. With weights 1, 2 and 3, which WMA(3) is correct?
options: $11.67, their unweighted mean.
$14 because the latest close has all the weight.
choiceFeedback: The SMA of these three closes is about $11.67. The WMA assigns unequal weights, so its arithmetic result must use 1, 2 and 3 explicitly.
The latest close gets the greatest weight but not all the weight. Earlier completed closes remain part of the weighted average.
modules.transferQuestion: A close jumps sharply while WMA and SMA share a lookback length. What is the defensible observation?
transferOptions: WMA usually reacts more because its newest close has greater weight.
Both averages must forecast the same future gain.
WMA identifies which institution executed the last trade.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Matching lookback periods do not make these averages predictive. Both are retrospective transformations of observed completed closes.
The WMA uses prices and predetermined weights, not trade-counterparty identities or evidence of institutional order flow.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: $12.33, or (10×1+11×2+14×3)÷6. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: WMA usually reacts more because its newest close has greater weight. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: For WMA(3), denominator 1+2+3=6. Multiply oldest close by 1 and newest by 3 before dividing; do not use a simple mean.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Percentage Price Oscillator (PPO)
modules.learn: PPO expresses the difference between a fast and slow EMA as a percentage of the slow EMA. This specific exercise plots the main PPO line, not a nine-period PPO signal line or histogram.
modules.why: A percentage-normalized EMA spread is easier to compare across securities with different nominal prices than a raw-dollar MACD line.
modules.method: Use completed close EMAs with declared 12- and 26-bar periods and consistent initialization. Compute PPO=100×(EMA12−EMA26)/EMA26. Require 26 completed closes and a nonzero denominator.
modules.limitation: PPO is not MACD in dollars, and a crossing does not automatically establish independent confirmation, profitable expectancy or a broker fill.
modules.question: If a completed-bar EMA12 is $10.40 and EMA26 is $10.00, what is the main PPO value?
options: 0.40 dollars, reported as a percentage.
Positive 40% because the averages are different.
choiceFeedback: $0.40 is the raw EMA spread. PPO rescales that difference by the slower EMA and reports a percentage, not dollars.
The difference is $0.40 out of $10.00, or 0.04 in ratio form; multiplying by 100 gives 4%, not 40%.
modules.transferQuestion: PPO rises while a close-based price invalidation is breached. What should Talia teach?
transferOptions: Positive PPO cancels the earlier invalidation.
PPO automatically establishes that a low-priced stock is undervalued.
Reassess under the original risk rule; PPO is secondary price-derived context.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A favorable derived indicator does not override a predeclared failed price structure or execution-risk limit.
PPO measures smoothed price relationships; it does not assess earnings, fair value, or intrinsic business worth.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Positive 4% from (10.40−10.00)÷10.00×100. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Reassess under the original risk rule; PPO is secondary price-derived context. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: PPO = 100 × (fast EMA − slow EMA)/slow EMA. Check which EMA belongs in the denominator and confirm 26 completed bars.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Stochastic Oscillator: Fast %K
modules.learn: Fast stochastic %K maps the last completed close to its position inside the highest-high/lowest-low range over the chosen N completed bars. It ranges from 0 to 100 when the range is nonzero.
modules.why: It helps separate where a close occurred within its recent range from claims about price direction, trend reversal, or whether a trade will fill.
modules.method: Compute %K=100×(close−lowest low N)/(highest high N−lowest low N). This activity shows raw fast %K, not the smoothed slow %K or %D signal line.
modules.limitation: At a zero high-low range the ratio is undefined, not an automatic buy/sell signal. An overbought reading can persist during a trend.
modules.question: Highest high is $110, lowest low is $100 and the completed close is $108. What is fast stochastic %K?
options: 80, because the close is eight of ten dollars above the range low.
108, because the close itself is the oscillator.
20, because only the distance from the upper high is counted.
choiceFeedback: The stochastic oscillator is scaled to the 0–100 range and uses the high-low window; it is not the raw closing price.
A distance of two from the upper extreme would correspond to 20% below the high, while %K measures 80% above the low.
modules.transferQuestion: The entire lookback window has equal highs and lows. Which response preserves calculation integrity?
transferOptions: Treat %K as 100 to force an overbought label.
Display insufficient range/undefined until a usable price window exists.
Assume the next price increase is certain.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A zero range makes the %K denominator zero. Labeling it 100 invents a signal with no mathematical basis.
A flat observed window cannot constrain the next trade; it only shows that the chosen data provided no usable stochastic range.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: 80, because the close is eight of ten dollars above the range low. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Display insufficient range/undefined until a usable price window exists. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Find the full highest-high minus lowest-low range, then locate close minus lowest-low within that range; do not use future bars or assume %D is displayed.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Williams %R: Range Position
modules.learn: Williams %R represents the current completed close's position within the N-bar high-low range using a negative scale from −100 to 0. It uses −100×(highest high−close)/(highest high−lowest low).
modules.why: It provides a complementary perspective on range-position momentum and shows that different display scales can describe the same completed-price location.
modules.method: Collect the highest high and lowest low of a declared set of completed bars; calculate −100×(high−close)/(high−low). Treat an exactly flat range as undefined rather than creating a false score.
modules.limitation: Williams %R is mathematically related to fast stochastic %K under equal windows; counting both as independent trade votes duplicates evidence.
modules.question: The completed close equals the highest high of a nonzero 14-bar range. What does Williams %R read?
options: −100, because price is at the upper bound.
0, because the distance from high to close is zero.
+100, because the next bar is certain to rise.
choiceFeedback: −100 corresponds to the close at the low of the declared range, not the top; check the sign and which distance is zero.
Williams %R uses a negative scale and describes historical location. A value of +100 is outside this definition and cannot forecast the next candle.
modules.transferQuestion: Stochastic %K and Williams %R seem to agree strongly. How should they affect confidence?
transferOptions: Treat them as mathematically related range-position evidence rather than two independent confirmations.
Two indicators guarantee twice the chance of a reversal.
Ignore whether their lookback windows are identical.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Both use the close's position relative to a rolling high-low window; duplicating the same input cannot independently double probability.
Different lookback windows can alter both values. Verify parameter parity before claiming agreement or divergence.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: 0, because the distance from high to close is zero. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Treat them as mathematically related range-position evidence rather than two independent confirmations. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Williams %R uses negative 100 times (highest high − close)/full range. At the highest high, the numerator is zero.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Average True Range Percent (ATRP)
modules.learn: ATRP divides a specified Average True Range by the latest completed closing price and expresses the result as a percentage. The ATR includes true range with prior-close gaps.
modules.why: ATRP helps compare observed movement magnitude across securities with different nominal price levels, while remaining direction-neutral.
modules.method: First calculate the chosen Wilder-smoothed ATR(N) from completed bars; then compute 100×ATR(N)/current completed close. State the warmup, price adjustment and nonzero denominator.
modules.limitation: ATRP is a volatility-context metric, not the spread or guaranteed maximum loss of a pending order. Illiquid execution may behave worse than the ATR.
modules.question: ATR(10) equals $0.50 and the completed close is $10.00. What is ATRP?
options: 50% because ATR reports an entire bar.
A 5% guaranteed adverse stop-fill ceiling.
choiceFeedback: $0.50 is five hundredths of the $10 close, not half of it. Multiply the ratio by 100 for the correct percentage.
ATRP is a retrospective volatility ratio. A market gap, halt or illiquid order can realize a worse result than any ATR multiple.
modules.transferQuestion: A $2 stock and a $200 stock each have $1 ATR. Which comparison is justified?
transferOptions: Their percentage volatility context must be equal.
The $200 stock is always more dangerous.
The $2 stock has a much higher ATRP, but execution risk still needs separate checks.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A $1 ATR is 50% of $2 but only 0.5% of $200. Dollar ATRs are not equal percentage movements.
A higher nominal price does not automatically imply larger ATRP or a particular stop-fill risk; use proportional calculations and quotes.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: 5% under 100×0.50/10.00. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: The $2 stock has a much higher ATRP, but execution risk still needs separate checks. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: ATRP is not just ATR. Divide ATR by the completed price, then multiply by 100. It measures historical magnitude, not fill certainty.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Average Volume: Completed-Bar SMA
modules.learn: Average volume is the arithmetic mean of share volume across a chosen number of comparable completed bars. This particular study uses N equally long fictional one-minute bars.
modules.why: It helps distinguish an unusually active bar from the local baseline while teaching why full-day totals and matched-time cumulative RVOL are different measures.
modules.method: Take the last N completed per-bar share volumes and divide their sum by N. Do not include an unfinished bar, a different market session or mixed bar durations.
modules.limitation: Average volume reveals share activity, not whether trades occurred at the bid or ask or who placed them. A high-volume bar is not a validated entry signal.
modules.question: Five comparable completed bars have 100, 200, 300, 200 and 200 shares. What is the five-bar average volume?
options: 1,000 shares, the total not the average.
100 shares, the smallest bar.
200 shares per completed bar, or 1,000÷5.
choiceFeedback: The sum is 1,000 shares across five bars. To estimate the average activity per bar, divide by the count of comparable completed bars.
The minimum observed bar is 100 shares, but a sample mean weights all five completed bars equally, not just the smallest.
modules.transferQuestion: A five-minute volume bar is compared with an average built from one-minute bars. What must be corrected?
transferOptions: Nothing; all volume counts share the same denominator.
Align interval and session definitions or aggregate comparably before interpreting a volume expansion.
Treat five-minute volume as institution-only activity.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A five-minute bar covers more time than a one-minute bar, so raw comparison may be inflated purely by differing durations.
Volume represents matched shares traded, not identified account types. A longer bar interval cannot prove who participated.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: 200 shares per completed bar, or 1,000÷5. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Align interval and session definitions or aggregate comparably before interpreting a volume expansion. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Average per-bar volume = sum of comparable, completed bar share counts ÷ number of bars, not total volume or directional volume.
modules.scope: Fictional completed one-minute OHLCV bars, source-defined calculations and no real trade, live quote, learner grade or future price.

modules.title: Choose the Research Security Universe
modules.learn: The scanner's security universe must be declared before evaluating price and volume. Exchange-listed common shares, ETFs, options and OTC securities have different conventions and eligibility.
modules.why: It prevents a familiar ticker symbol or a strong chart from silently substituting a different asset or exchange venue.
modules.method: For this fictional lesson, require a verified common-share class on the declared listed universe; reject a candidate with an incompatible instrument or an unverified listing.
modules.limitation: The website's fictional universe flags are not current exchange listings or a brokerage eligibility check; live class validation needs primary identifiers.
modules.question: A candidate matches the price filter but is an option contract in a common-stock-only universe. What follows?
options: Include it because the ticker looks familiar.
Exclude it until instrument identity fits the declared universe.
A larger RVOL cancels the universe definition.
choiceFeedback: A similar ticker stem does not make an option contract a listed common share; underlying and derivative identities remain distinct.
Unusual activity cannot change an option into a common share. Universe selection is independent of volume ranking.
modules.transferQuestion: A ticker symbol is reassigned to a different issuer in the historical period being studied. What should the research process do?
transferOptions: Reconcile issuer, security class and effective date before interpreting historical charts.
Assume all ticker histories belong to the current issuer.
Use a moving average to identify historical corporate ownership.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Tickers can change or be reused. A present-day symbol is not sufficient evidence that past trading data belong to the same legal security.
Indicators calculate from prices; they cannot resolve a company's legal security identifiers or historical listing chronology.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: Exclude it until instrument identity fits the declared universe. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Reconcile issuer, security class and effective date before interpreting historical charts. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: First declare the instrument family and listing universe. Scanner criteria cannot waive an incompatible share class.

modules.title: Corporate Actions and Security Identity
modules.learn: Historical charts and watchlists must reconcile splits, reverse splits and share-class changes before treating past prices and current float numbers as comparable.
modules.why: A dramatic price jump can be a corporate-action adjustment rather than genuine market appreciation or a new catalyst.
modules.method: Use dated issuer/security identity, the effective split ratio and a consistent raw/adjusted price basis for this fictional stock.
modules.limitation: An adjusted chart may not equal the contemporaneous raw trade price; share counts and float estimates can also have different effective dates.
modules.question: A 1-for-10 reverse split changes nominal shares and price per share. Can an unadjusted 900% chart jump be called ordinary demand?
options: Yes, because every nominal increase is a positive return.
Yes, if a one-minute RSI is above 70.
No; reconcile split adjustment and issuer identity before judging the price move.
choiceFeedback: A reverse split changes the nominal share count and price scale. The unadjusted jump is not by itself a tradable total-return gain.
RSI cannot repair a corporate-action mismatch. First bring historical data and share identifiers onto a comparable basis.
modules.transferQuestion: A historical runner had a small reported float before a later offering. Which source question matters?
transferOptions: Use only the most recent float for all dates.
Verify the float and outstanding shares effective at each historical pause.
Treat the offering as proof the prior breakout was filled.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Current share count may reflect later offerings and splits that were unknown in the earlier period. Using it retrospectively leaks later facts.
Issuer financing events cannot prove the entry or execution of an earlier hypothetical trade, even if later price paths are known.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: No; reconcile split adjustment and issuer identity before judging the price move. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Verify the float and outstanding shares effective at each historical pause. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Separate raw contemporaneous prices from adjusted charts and date-stamp both issuer identity and share-count changes.

modules.title: Premarket, Prior-Day and Live Price Levels
modules.learn: A watchlist can include premarket high, completed prior-day high, current high of day and VWAP, but each reference has its own session, update time and source.
modules.why: This makes price-level alerts testable while preventing a future session high from being used to justify an earlier entry.
modules.method: Record each fictional reference's session boundary and whether it was known at the actual replay pause. Only completed reference levels qualify.
modules.limitation: HOD can evolve intraday; PDH depends on the completed previous declared session; a price touching a reference does not prove breakout acceptance.
modules.question: A stock makes a new high later in the day. Can the later HOD be used as an earlier morning resistance level?
options: Yes, all daily highs are known from the opening bell.
No, use only the highest price observed as of the earlier pause.
Yes, a scanner alert proves when the later HOD formed.
choiceFeedback: A full-day high is known only after the high occurs. Borrowing it into an earlier decision violates time-order discipline.
An alert can fire at a price condition, but it does not authorize using a subsequently discovered high at an earlier clock time.
modules.transferQuestion: An unfinished premarket bar appears to exceed the declared PMH. What is the defensible response under a completed-bar rule?
transferOptions: Wait for the declared completed-bar trigger and verify the premarket session.
Treat the unfinished wick as guaranteed acceptance.
Use tomorrow's high to confirm today's pause.
transferFeedbackByChoice: A bar still in progress may retract before completion. The defined confirmation rule has not yet been observed.
A future day's high is not information available at the present decision pause; it cannot validate a current trigger.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: No, use only the highest price observed as of the earlier pause. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Wait for the declared completed-bar trigger and verify the premarket session. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: For every level, name session, timestamp and whether the reference was already observed; distinguish live HOD from completed prior-day high.

modules.title: Multi-Timeframe Confirmation and Bar Completion
modules.learn: Daily context, five-minute setup and one-minute execution timing answer distinct questions. A one-minute breakout cannot stand in for a required unfinished five-minute confirmation.
modules.why: Separating timeframes reduces hindsight and prevents a fast alert from overruling the rule that actually governs the trade.
modules.method: Treat one-minute timing as secondary; require the five-minute setup bar to be completed and the higher-timeframe context dated for this fictional lane.
modules.limitation: Timeframe alignment does not guarantee the direction of the next candle or solve spread, halt and liquidity problems.
modules.question: A one-minute bar briefly breaks resistance while the five-minute setup candle remains unfinished. What should Talia classify?
options: Confirmed on every timeframe.
The observed one-minute event is not yet the required completed five-minute setup.
A market order has already filled at the breakout level.
choiceFeedback: The faster interval can show a preliminary move, but the defined five-minute bar confirmation has not finished.
A candle touching a level is not an acknowledged broker order. Price evidence does not prove any order was placed or filled.
modules.transferQuestion: The daily trend is strong but a predeclared five-minute invalidation is reached. What rule governs the short-horizon setup?
transferOptions: A strong daily trend cancels the written intraday risk rule.
The trade must automatically reverse short.
The original setup invalidation and execution restrictions still matter.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Longer-horizon context cannot silently remove the short-horizon plan's written invalidation or position-risk limit.
The failure of a long-side setup does not automatically establish a valid, borrowable short-side order.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: The observed one-minute event is not yet the required completed five-minute setup. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: The original setup invalidation and execution restrictions still matter. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Write the purpose of each timeframe before looking: daily context, five-minute setup, one-minute timing. Only completed required evidence qualifies.

modules.title: Hard Risk Vetoes versus Candidate Scores
modules.learn: A watchlist rank can organize research quality, but a high explanatory score cannot compensate for unresolved security identity, source freshness, halt, borrowing or excessive spread.
modules.why: Keeping hard risk gates separate prevents a collection of favorable indicators from being treated as permission to trade an ineligible instrument.
modules.method: Score source quality and chart clarity in a fictional 0–100 exercise, then independently reject any candidate with an unresolved critical risk field.
modules.limitation: The score is an illustrative sorting heuristic, not a probability of success or a license to override real broker restrictions.
modules.question: Candidate A scores 95/100 but fails the written maximum spread. Which decision is defensible?
options: High score makes the spread threshold optional.
NO TRADE for that setup; hard cost veto wins.
Price movement later proves the score was a valid entry.
choiceFeedback: An educational ranking measures soft factors. It cannot change the execution-cost rule that was declared as mandatory.
Hindsight returns cannot establish that the earlier executable price and risk conditions existed when the decision was made.
modules.transferQuestion: Candidate B scores 68 but passes documented hard gates, while C scores 98 with unresolved identity. What should be prioritized?
transferOptions: C must always rank ahead, regardless of identity.
Both are guaranteed entries.
B can proceed to further research while C remains in verification despite its higher score.
transferFeedbackByChoice: An invalid or unverified security identity prevents reliable price and risk measurements. High rank is not a substitute for traceable identity.
Passing eligibility is still not a guaranteed entry; both candidates require separate setup and position-risk review.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: NO TRADE for that setup; hard cost veto wins. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: B can proceed to further research while C remains in verification despite its higher score. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Keep mandatory source, borrow, halt, spread and identity vetoes outside the scoring function. A weighted score is not a permission gate.

modules.title: Reproducible Dynamic Scanner Snapshots
modules.learn: A dynamic scanner changes as prices, corporate actions and source status update. Research must freeze the exact scan configuration and event time before evaluating later outcomes.
modules.why: Versioned snapshots enable an honest audit of what was visible at the actual time instead of reconstructing candidates from future winners.
modules.method: For this fictional batch, require a captured query version and time-stamped candidate row. Uncaptured/expired versions must return to research pending verification.
modules.limitation: A screenshot or CSV can omit delayed quote provenance; a reproducible scan also needs its universe, filters, data source and revision.
modules.question: After a rally, an analyst runs today's scanner and claims every winner was on yesterday's list. What evidence is needed?
options: A frozen timestamped previous-day scan/query and candidate inclusion record.
Only the winner's latest chart and one screenshot.
A successful later trade automatically proves the earlier scan result.
choiceFeedback: A future-selected chart cannot reconstruct the actual earlier set of scanner inclusions, exclusions or data delays.
Later profit does not establish that a stock met the original scan criteria before the movement occurred.
modules.transferQuestion: A watchlist query changed from version 1 to version 2 after the replay pause. How should performance comparisons be handled?
transferOptions: Merge both rule sets without recording which was used.
Use versioned before-outcome snapshots and compare each cohort under its actual rules.
Retrospectively assign the better-performing version to every winner.
transferFeedbackByChoice: Mixing version 1 and version 2 makes the selection rule irreproducible and can hide changes in risk or universe constraints.
Reassigning a later successful rule to previous candidates is hindsight optimization; it destroys a genuine chronological audit.
modules.feedback: The evidence supports: A frozen timestamped previous-day scan/query and candidate inclusion record. This is an ungraded interpretation of observed fictional data, not an instruction to place an order.
modules.transferFeedback: The changed case supports: Use versioned before-outcome snapshots and compare each cohort under its actual rules. Recheck the evidence and the original source/risk rules before taking action.
modules.scaffold: Freeze universe, filters, source timestamps, candidate rows and query-version ID before revealing outcomes. No snapshot means no reproducible claim.
